Definition: from G1909 and G424; to come up on, i.e. return:--come again, return.
BiblicalUsage: To come again, to return. The good Samaritan tells the host that when he comes again he will repay whatever more is spent in Luke 10:35, and the nobleman returns having received the kingdom in Luke 19:15 to call his servants to account.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Lord who went away will come again, and the account will be settled then — what I spent on the wounded traveller will be repaid.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
